question: Who is remembered as the pioneer of mitosis research and the founder of cytogenetics?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Walther Flemming.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• German anatomist **Walther Flemming **is credited with founding the field of **cytogenetics**.
 
• He was the first to systematically study and describe how **chromosomes **behave in the **cell nucleus **during typical **cell division **(mitosis).
 
• Flemming held appointments at the **Universities **of **Prague **and **Kiel **after serving as a **military doctor **during the Franco-German War (1876–1901).
 
• He discovered in **1879 **that a certain family of **dyes **revealed a **threadlike substance **in the **nucleus**.
 
• He was a pioneer in the use of newly discovered aniline dyes to see **cell architecture**.
 
• He created a series of slides by applying these stains to cells destroyed at various stages of **cell division**, establishing the sequence of changes that occur in the nucleus during cell division under a **microscope**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Martin Evans:**

 
 
• **​**In 1981, Sir Martin John Evans, an **English researcher**, and **Matthew Kaufman **became the first to develop **mouse embryonic stem cells **in a lab.
 
• Along with **Mario Capecchi **and **Oliver Smithies**, he is renowned for his work on the development of the knockout mouse and the associated gene targeting technology, which uses **embryonic stem cells **to **alter **particular **mouse genes**.
 
 
 
• **Pierre Joseph Pelletier:**
 
 
• **​French scientist **and **pharmacist **Pierre-Joseph Pelletier co-discovered **quinine**, **caffeine**, and **strychnine **with Joseph Bienaimé Caventou.
 
• Pelletier is known for his work on **vegetable alkaloids**.
 
 
 
• **Albert Von Kolliker:**
 
 
• **Swiss anatomist**, **physiologist**, and **histologist **Albert von Kölliker was born at Zurich on the 6th of July 1817.
